commits.message:
feat(cli): `npx wizards` downloads a small launcher; the runtime is published as @engenty/wizards-runtime (#39)

## In short

`npx wizards` used to take about **2 minutes** before the first setup question. It downloaded the whole app (about **776 MB**) just to start the installer, and the installer then downloaded the same app a second time.

Now `npx wizards` downloads a **17 KB** starter program. That program runs the installer right away, so the app is downloaded only once.

## What changes for people

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| First download of `npx wizards` | ~776 MB | ~17 KB |
| Downloads of the app | 2 | 1 |
| `curl … install.sh \| bash` | unchanged | unchanged |
| Existing installs | – | keep working and keep updating themselves |

## How it works

We now publish two npm packages instead of one:

- **`wizards`**: the small starter `npx wizards` runs. It installs engenty wizards and passes every command on to the installed program.
- **`@engenty/wizards-runtime`** (new): the actual app, which the installer and the automatic updates download.

**Existing installs:** an install on 0.7.4 or older updates itself by downloading `wizards`, which is now the starter. When the starter finds it has landed inside an install, it downloads the real app and starts it, so the update still finishes on its own. It was tested with a real 0.7.2 install; 0.7.3 and 0.7.4 update the same way.

## Tested

- A fresh `npx wizards` installs and starts; `--version` and `mcp` work.
- A 0.7.2 install updates itself to the new version, and `npx wizards` brings a 0.7.2 install up to date.
- All automated tests, lint and type checks pass. The release workflow now checks these cases too.

## Needed before the next release

1. **The npm token (`NPM_TOKEN`) must be allowed to publish `@engenty/wizards-runtime`.** It's a new package, and the release fails at the npm step without this.
2. **The desktop app** (not in this repo): if it installs `wizards` by name, it has to switch to `@engenty/wizards-runtime`.

## Small trade-offs

- With nothing installed yet, the first `npx wizards --help`, `validate` or `mcp` installs engenty wizards first (about a minute). CI can still validate without installing: `npx -p @engenty/wizards-runtime wizards validate …`.
- An older install that updates this way keeps no previous version to go back to. It still works normally.

---

commits.message:
feat(cli): auto-update the installed wizards in the background (#34)

An install made by install.sh keeps one folder per version (runtime/<version>/ with a `current` link, and runtime/node_modules linked to current for older commands). The runtime asks the npm registry for the newest wizards at start and once a day and installs a newer one beside the running version; npm checks its integrity. `wizards start` switches to it before any runtime runs, so at a restart or the next login, never mid-run. The previous version is kept.

`wizards status` and the studio banner say "Updated to X" with what changed, or that X is downloaded. Off with `wizards autoupdate off` or WIZARDS_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE=1; off by default in CI and for installs set up without a terminal. npx and checkouts never update themselves.

commits.message:
feat(results): agent steps return nested data through output.schema

- packages/shared/src/shape.ts (FSL-1.1-MIT OR MIT) describes a json step's
  data in the project's own kinds: text, number, yesno, choice, ref, and lists
  of these or of entries with lists of their own, each with a label; at most
  four levels deep and a hundred keys; a ref points at a top-level list whose
  entries have an id.
- output.fields compile to the same shape (stepShape): one code path builds
  the model's strict JSON Schema (draft 2020-12), fits and checks the agent's
  own JSON, keeps lists as lists and stores the nested data.
- validateSurface follows a view's paths through repeated entries and Link
  views into the schema; optionsFrom, cards and conditions read top-level
  lists of entries.
- Downloads: xlsx one sheet per top-level list, csv the first list of flat
  entries, md and pdf the whole tree.
- The admin's data editor (Ansicht · Bearbeiten · JSON) shows and edits a
  json step's output in reviews with edit and in the studio's run drawers
  (PUT /api/runs/:id/outputs/:stepId, checked against the schema); a ⋮ menu
  there and on the step in the editor shows, copies or downloads the JSON
  Schema.
- Authoring guide: the schema, and the view first, then the schema it needs.
  JSON Schema v1 regenerated; output-schema.test.ts runs Kühlschrank-Koch
  end to end.

Runs carry `run.lang`: the view shows the translation, AI steps write in that language, a switch mid-run keeps what is made, a finished result can be translated (`state.translated`). Authors turn it off per wizard (`wizard.translate`, synced to the cloud copy) and correct a language line by line in Share → Settings. "The wizard doesn't match the schema." goes through the runtime's string table (ServerLine on NotedError)

commits.message:
refactor(knowledge)!: English names in the source for Wissen and its parts; packages keep pages under files/knowledge/ (#13)

## Why

The code names (functions, types, files) already said `knowledge` and
`categories`, but the German UI terms had crept into comments, the text
the AI steps and the studio assistant read, a few object keys, and the
English translations.

## What changes

| German | English |
|---|---|
| Wissen | Knowledge |
| Kategorie / Kategorien | category / categories |
| Übersicht | summary |
| Inhaltsverzeichnis | table of contents |
| Info & Marke, Daten, Ergebnisse | Info & brand, Data, Results |

What the model sees:
- The steps' block is headed `# KNOWLEDGE — WHAT THE SPACE KNOWS`, and
the project_* / page_read tool descriptions say Knowledge and
categories.
- `page_read` front matter says `categories:` instead of `kategorien:`.
So do the `project_search` / `project_list` results and the relevance
check's candidates.
- The studio assistant's space state is `knowledge` / `categories`. Its
prompt still says the German studio calls it „Wissen“, so it can follow
German-speaking people.
- New summary units in the index are titled `— Summary`. Units already
in the index keep `— Übersicht` until they are rebuilt.

Two bugs fixed:
- The English studio showed "Kategorie", "Kategorien", "New Kategorie",
"Delete Kategorie" and "What are Kategorien for?".
- Reading a website reported "Schreibt die Seiten in Wissen …" and
"Liest die Angaben …" for English sites too. Both lines now follow the
site's language, like the line before them.

## Package folder
Breaking: a package now keeps the space's pages under `files/knowledge/`
instead of `files/wissen/` (`KNOWLEDGE_DIR` in `services/package.ts`).
Matthias agreed: no legacy support. The WordPress plugin reads
`knowledge/` from its next release
(engenty/engenty-wizards-wp-plugin#2).

## Not changed
- German translations and German error messages, German example data in
tests and tool hints, and the German stopword list.
- `docs/plans/`, the changelogs and `TODO.md`.

## Testing
- `pnpm typecheck` and `biome check` on the changed files pass.
- Runtime tests: 506 passed, 5 skipped. Tests that assert on renamed
strings and keys are updated (`knowledge.test.ts`, `space-data.test.ts`,
`api-v1.test.ts`, `assistant.test.ts`).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---------

commits.message:
ci: 2x faster checks: side by side, TypeScript 7, cached docs build and test timings (#14)

Makes CI faster: **~4 min → ~2 min per run** (≈240s → 124s on this PR,
with every cache cold; later runs should come in lower).

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Whole run | ~240s | 124s |
| Typecheck | 49–52s | 14s |
| Test | 73–76s | 72s (timings cache cold) |
| Build | 36–38s | 11s |
| Docs | 31–33s | 33s (Next cache cold) |

## Changes

1. **Checks side by side.** `verify` is now four parallel jobs:
`typecheck` (with lint), `test`, `build`, `docs`. `deploy` still waits
for all of them. Check names become `verify (typecheck)` etc.; nothing
on `main` requires the old name.
2. **TypeScript 7** for runtime, web, shared, plugin-sdk, the run-log
example and the root. `apps/docs` and `packages/runner` stay on
TypeScript 6: Next.js and `vite-plugin-dts` load TypeScript as a
library, which 7 no longer offers. Docs' `tsconfig.json` drops `baseUrl`
so it's ready to follow. The runtime's build output is byte-identical to
TypeScript 6; `packages/shared`'s `.d.ts` only list some members in
another order.
3. **Docs build cache.** The docs job keeps `apps/docs/.next/cache`
between runs.
4. **Test timings cache.** vitest's per-file durations are kept between
runs, so `sandbox.test.ts` (~39s) starts first instead of last – the
test job should drop toward ~50s from the next run on.

Lint, typecheck, test, build and the docs build pass locally
(`apple.test.ts` fails only on a Mac with the helper built – a stale
expectation unrelated to this change, fixed separately).

auto-installed and brought Expo, React Native and Babel (395 packages)
into every install – and into the runtime image's production install. An
override (`drizzle-orm>expo-sqlite: "-"`) leaves it out; no other
package changes its version, nothing is added.

alone and type-checks it there; the other checks install everything but
the docs site.

what fetching everything from the registry takes, so it is dropped
rather than split per check.

typecheck, test (66 files), build, docs typecheck and build.

commits.message: English names in the source for Wissen and its parts; packages keep pages under files/knowledge/ (#13)
commits.body:
## Why

The code names (functions, types, files) already said `knowledge` and
`categories`, but the German UI terms had crept into comments, the text
the AI steps and the studio assistant read, a few object keys, and the
English translations.

## What changes

| German | English |
|---|---|
| Wissen | Knowledge |
| Kategorie / Kategorien | category / categories |
| Übersicht | summary |
| Inhaltsverzeichnis | table of contents |
| Info & Marke, Daten, Ergebnisse | Info & brand, Data, Results |

What the model sees:
- The steps' block is headed `# KNOWLEDGE — WHAT THE SPACE KNOWS`, and
the project_* / page_read tool descriptions say Knowledge and
categories.
- `page_read` front matter says `categories:` instead of `kategorien:`.
So do the `project_search` / `project_list` results and the relevance
check's candidates.
- The studio assistant's space state is `knowledge` / `categories`. Its
prompt still says the German studio calls it „Wissen“, so it can follow
German-speaking people.
- New summary units in the index are titled `— Summary`. Units already
in the index keep `— Übersicht` until they are rebuilt.

Two bugs fixed:
- The English studio showed "Kategorie", "Kategorien", "New Kategorie",
"Delete Kategorie" and "What are Kategorien for?".
- Reading a website reported "Schreibt die Seiten in Wissen …" and
"Liest die Angaben …" for English sites too. Both lines now follow the
site's language, like the line before them.

## Package folder
Breaking: a package now keeps the space's pages under `files/knowledge/`
instead of `files/wissen/` (`KNOWLEDGE_DIR` in `services/package.ts`).
Matthias agreed: no legacy support. The WordPress plugin reads
`knowledge/` from its next release
(engenty/engenty-wizards-wp-plugin#2).

## Not changed
- German translations and German error messages, German example data in
tests and tool hints, and the German stopword list.
- `docs/plans/`, the changelogs and `TODO.md`.

## Testing
- `pnpm typecheck` and `biome check` on the changed files pass.
- Runtime tests: 506 passed, 5 skipped. Tests that assert on renamed
strings and keys are updated (`knowledge.test.ts`, `space-data.test.ts`,
`api-v1.test.ts`, `assistant.test.ts`).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commits.body:
* feat(i18n): English is the base language everywhere, and the studio speaks the language the person picked instead of the browser's – requests carry the pick, numbers and dates follow it, the editor's hard-coded German moved into the dictionary, and the server's messages say both languages and answer in the asker's

- English is the base: the dictionaries are keyed by English, German is the translation; a request, runner or first visit without a language gets English; a wizard that is not clearly German counts as English; plugin starters without a language are English (docs say so); a WordPress site gets German only for a German locale

- The connection popup speaks the picked language: it rides the sealed OAuth state; plugins pass it with connections.start({ lang })
- The authoring guide's example wizard and the WordPress import prompt are English

commits.message: the account becomes the front door – a cloud studio's first visit is a wizard of four pages (the team's name, the website read into the space, first documents, the space explained), the setup on a computer starts with the account (a device code in the terminal, the panel and "engenty credits" as an engine on the setup page), install.sh --local and wizards account keep and name the install without one, the cloud home offers the computer with the install mail, and the docs start with "Create an account"
commits.body:
- services/onboarding.ts: needsOnboarding (managed, owner or admin, no mark, no wizard yet), finishOnboarding, applyWebsite (readWebsite into name, about, three colours and the logo, without a model); routes PUT /team, POST /onboarding/done, POST /projects/:id/website, POST /install-mail; /me answers onboarding and the account's team; manage.ts renameTenant and installMail (contract: PATCH /v1/tenants/:id, POST /v1/install-mail)
- studio: /start (OnboardingPage), the redirect in App.tsx, the setup page's account panel and credits choice, the cloud home's "Also on your computer", footers say engenty
- CLI: the account step first in wizards setup (auth/device.ts: device code, polled at the token endpoint, kept like the browser flow), wizards account status | sign-in | sign-out, --local writes account=off and local: true, install-env.ts points the CLI at the install before env.ts runs (it used to make a data folder wherever it was called), English callback and error strings
- docs: create-account.md, local-only.md, the user guide reordered, README; plan docs/plans/cloud-first-onboarding.md with the mockups and what was built

commits.message: feat(runtime): the runner is its own process – RUNTIME_ROLE web | runner | all (a runtime that runs alone stays one process). The line of runs lives in the control database: run_index gained owner and seen, a runner claims a run in one statement that counts the tenant's held runs against its limit, reports every 10 s, hears of a cancel the web wrote and hands its runs back when it stops; a runner silent for 30 s loses them. A step's question and the person's answer go through the run's row (run.answer; run.unattended marks an autopilot), so the web that takes the answer need not be the process that asked. watchRun tells the stream, the autopilot and waitWhileMoving of changes another process made within a second. Runners register with an address (table runner, RUNNER_URL); the web hands a run's browser screen and acts on it to the runner holding it. compose.cloud.yaml runs web and runner apart. docs/plans/runner-process.md

fix: a live conversation only where the wizard has it on, the browser the setup found, plugin runs without device signals, the WordPress plugin's download

- The chat's phone button, the call screen and POST /api/runs/:id/talk open a live
  conversation only where the wizard has live voice or the video call switched on; the owner's
  test run always may (engine/runner.ts talkAllowed). Before, any visitor could start one on the
  owner's OpenAI key once a key was set.
- The runtime starts the browser the setup and `wizards doctor` report: CHROME_PATH, else the
  first Chrome, Edge, Chromium or Brave found (render/browser-path.ts, used by env.ts and
  cli/machine.ts). Before, the setup counted Edge, Chromium or Brave while PDF, PNG and website
  steps only looked for Google Chrome or /usr/bin/chromium.
- A plugin's runs.subscribe no longer gets the device requests as a run change with no event.
- The plugin build scans packages/runner/src/ui.tsx too, where most of the studio's components
  live now, so their classes are in a plugin's own layer again.
- The WordPress plugin's download points at engenty/engenty-wizards-wp-plugin (the old address
  answered 404); the shortcode sample on Settings → Integrate follows the studio's language.
- `wizards report` without an account names Settings → Account; the setup's Apple hint and the
  harness messages name the Models section, not "Models & account".

commits.message:
fix: Apple Intelligence leaves High and Highest on their way, a visitor reads the runtime's answers in their language

- Picking Apple Intelligence binds only Classifier and Standard to it and keeps the source: an
  installed client, an own key or the credits stay the way of High and Highest (models.ts
  ownRef takes an apple: binding first under any source; Models and the setup send only the
  two bindings, and picking a client or the credits unbinds them). Before, the pick switched
  the source to own keys and High and Highest lost the client or the credits.
- Voice notes on the Mac no longer show "switched off" when only Apple Intelligence is off:
  transcription needs macOS 26 and the helper, not Apple Intelligence.
- A visitor's route answers (not available, the day's limit, run over, live talk off, sizes,
  closed questions, links gone, …) come from RUN_NOTES in the request's language, as the
  runner's interface; Apple's and the conversation's errors in a run are notes too, so the
  runner shows them in its language (NotedError in model-errors.ts).

commits.message:
Merge claude/pdf-in-browser – the standalone runner (packages/runner), the check of what a wizard needs on a site without an account (fit.ts), the API the WordPress plugin calls and a written output's PDF made in the browser, onto main

Main moved on for 86 commits meanwhile; what changed where both worked:
- the runner package takes main's live browser (browser-live.tsx), the on-device transcription of a voice note, the cards' words, Tabs and the dialog that keeps its height; the chat view imports its pieces from the package
- createApi tells the host of a 5xx (RunnerEnv.onServerError), so the studio's log still gets them
- embed.js keeps main's chat popout and the bubble the WordPress plugin writes, both with data-page; the share dialog offers steps or chat, in the page, behind a button or as a bubble
- run.origin is tenant migration 0013 after main's 0011/0012
- the website import's assistant part runs the studio assistant, which replaced the project assistant
- release.yml: the runner archive's dist folder is made first

commits.message: the assistant stands on every studio page but the editor, with one chat per person and team – docked at the bottom (opened, it greets with the page's words and three suggestions; a click sends one, a "fill" one goes into the field), small at the lower right (Data and Results keep it so) or as a sidebar on a window of 1,520 px and more, kept per person (GET/PUT /api/studio/assistant/layout); its height is kept free below the page (--assistant-dock), which fixes the last section under the bar; the chat is stored (assistant_chat, assistant_message, FTS5 trigrams), survives pages, reloads and devices, "New chat" closes it with a dense summary by the standard model, the last five summaries ride every turn, chats_search and chat_read find older ones, a long chat folds into a running summary; it knows the app from the guides of the installed version (docs/content bundled into dist/docs, docs_search, docs_read, the authoring guide, a one-page primer) and reads live data (gallery, plans from the Manage-App's public GET /v1/plans, account, usage per month via GET /v1/tenants/:id/usage or /v1/me/usage, the space's wizards and runs, models); every message carries the page's snapshot (route, trail, section in view, open item, selection, summary, fields; useAssistantPage, studio.useAssistantPage), and six browser tools run in the page while the turn stays open (navigate, highlight with spotlight or ring and a card whose buttons answer, look_at_page, read_section, fill_field, scroll_to; studio.useAssistantTool adds a page's own) – the same for an installed client over the MCP bridge, own keys and credits; the turn's events keep our SSE names with AG-UI's fields (run_started, text with messageId, tool_call and tool_result for every tool, card, changed, done, error); Talk starts a live chat the browser's way: speech to text in the browser (recording and the voice-notes model where it cannot), a pause sends, the same assistant answers, the computer's voices or the speech model read it aloud, talking over it stops it; studio.Assistant now only tells the assistant what to say on a plugin's page; user guide page "The assistant", plugin guide and the Manage contract updated

commits.message: feat(debug): a look from afar at every installation – every process keeps the last 3000 lines it printed in memory (log.ts: the console is hooked once, each line still goes where it went, keys, tokens, JWTs and one-time links are taken out before a line is kept). The runtime answers about itself in debug.ts, read-only and never with a key: status, logs, one run of any tenant with its error and events, where a tenant's classes run. The Manage-App reaches it over /api/internal/debug/* with the service key; the command line of a local install over /api/local/debug/* with a ticket (wizards logs, wizards report – status, model settings without keys and the last 500 lines go to the account's /v1/diagnostics only when the person runs it). A page in a browser sends the errors it meets to POST /api/log, capped and rate-limited, so the studio's side shows in the same log. The raw words of an installed AI client's failure are logged before they are summed up for the person. docs/plans/remote-debug.md

commits.message: feat(plugins): Pro modules on a local install – the closed plugins the linked account's plan includes come from its Manage-App (/v1/modules) as zips signed for the release, checked against the public key the runtime ships with before anything is unpacked, and installed into <DATA_DIR>/pro-modules apart from the person's plugins; they load only while the entitlement the Manage-App signed lists them, belongs to the linked account and has not ended (a week offline), and only in the release they were built for, are fetched anew for a new release or build, and go off with the plan or the account while their files and tables stay; Settings → Plugins has a Pro modules section (install, update, remove, check the plan) and stays reachable for a linked account without plugins; concurrent refreshes of the account token share one request, so the start-up checks no longer refuse each other

commits.message: feat(plugins): what a booking plugin needs from the runtime – a plugin connects accounts of the space itself (server.connections: start, list, call, remove, with the shared sign-in callback and token refresh), brings starters to the marketplace (registerStarter), learns whether a step runs as a test (step.mode) and in which wizard, and tells the space assistant what its own page holds (registerAssistantContext), where the assistant now stands docked (studio.Assistant) and the page names its place in the top bar's trail (studio.useCrumbs); a page field of kind slot offers free times as chips by day; the studio has a date picker and a date range picker, a composer shared by every chat (a pill on one line, the buttons level with the text, a menu beside the mic to choose the microphone and to hold to record) that floats docked over a blurred band clear of a phone's home bar, and a page menu that slides one level down at the side and becomes tabs on a phone; Google Calendar and Outlook events take a location, Google's an invitation to send and Outlook lists every event with its free/busy; the first slash of the trail stands as close to the wordmark as the others

commits.message: feat: a field can be shown only under a condition – it appears as the person answers another field of the same page, or depends on anything known before the page – and a hidden field is neither required nor kept; the choices of a select can come from earlier data (a list an AI step found, a column of its table, or a column of a list the wizard keeps), with the fixed choices standing in while that data is empty; branches compare numbers (greater, less), look into multiselects, lists and texts (contains), read how many rows a kept list has, and take several conditions that must all hold; the studio edits a field's condition and the source of its choices, the diagram labels the new conditions, and the assistant is told to use conditions instead of one copy of a page per answer

commits.message: feat: the AI can decide how a wizard goes on and which questions it asks – a branch can carry a statement instead of a condition ("the person wants a refund") and all such branches of a step are decided together in one small call, a field can be shown when the AI finds a statement true and fields of a group are alternatives of which it shows the one that fits, decided once as the run reaches the page; every decision goes to a decision model where there is a way to one (Jev through the credits, an AI Gateway key or a TypeSafe key) and otherwise to the classifier class's language model, so decision steps now carry how probable their answers are (branches read it as steps.<id>.<field>.p) and Wissen's relevance check works without Jev; decision steps answer scores on a scale; a branch back to an earlier step is a loop that stops after its max (ten without one) and the step that runs again sees what it made last time; an AI step can run once per row of a table or a kept list and hands on one table of the results

commits.message:
feat: a wizard can make a film with Claude Code: the new step type "film" lets the AI client installed on this computer write a motion-graphics film as code in a folder of its own – with HyperFrames' skills (fetched once from GitHub at a pinned version), the wizard's style kit (a .zip in its workspace, unpacked as the bar to reach), the space's brand (name, colours named by use, facts, logos) and the run's material (voice, script, pictures, uploads) – and the runtime renders the MP4 with HyperFrames (installed into the data folder on the first film); the client's shell runs in its sandbox, writing only inside the folder and without network, and reaches HyperFrames' render, snapshots and checks through a tool of the step limited to the folder; sounds come only from a catalog of CC0 effects (soundcn by Kenney, HyperFrames' own); a film runs only where Claude Code is the AI subscription, never on credits or in the cloud, the runner says so before a run starts and the marketplace shows it as a capability; a film that stops picks up the client's session on the next try, a failed final render goes back to the client to fix, and a review's note changes the film's code instead of making it again; the folder goes with the run's files

Also: a recording a file field listens to is written down piece by piece between its pauses with exact times ({{field.speech}}); film widgets play sound from a second of its source on up to 48 tracks and mix sounds from the workspace; widget data gets the pictures an agent step kept; a voice step's style is a template; a review no longer shows a step a branch skipped; the plan is in docs/plans/motion-graphics-wizards.md

feat: MCP endpoint for authoring wizards with personal API keys

Admins build and change wizards from their own MCP clients. /api/mcp
(stateless Streamable HTTP, official SDK v2) offers 14 tools: authoring
guide, starters, projects, wizards, validate, create, edit ops, replace,

document preview frame renders again.

commits.message:
feat: OAuth sign-in for MCP clients, connected apps in settings

MCP clients connect without a key: they discover /api/mcp (RFC 9728),
register themselves (dynamic registration or a client metadata
document), the admin signs in and allows access on /consent, and the
client gets a token bound to /api/mcp. Tools follow the granted scopes.
Settings list connected apps; disconnecting removes the consent and the
tokens and cuts the app off at once. Personal API keys keep working.

Registrations with only loopback or custom-scheme redirects count as
native apps, so clients that leave application_type out still connect.

Includes migration 0002 of the workspace work, which 0003 builds on.

commits.message:
feat: live studio — MCP and other edits show up without a reload

The editor subscribes to /api/studio/wizards/:id/stream. Every draft
write (studio, architect, MCP client) announces its revision and the
steps it touched; the editor fetches the new state, the changed steps
pulse in the diagram and the header names the client. Notes left by an
MCP client appear in the thread between turns.

Inspector edits still unsaved when another write lands are never lost:
their save meets the newer revision, the edits merge step by step onto
it (studio wins on the same step) and save again.

commits.message:
feat: interactive widgets with a workspace per wizard, shareable results

Widgets are HTML apps written once into the wizard's workspace; a widget
step only binds each run's data into them — no model call, same look
every run. The result is one self-contained HTML file (scripts, styles,
images and reference data inlined) that previews, downloads and renders
to PNG, PDF and MP4 (the widget's timeline stepped frame by frame in
Chromium, encoded with ffmpeg). Widgets talk to the platform through
window.wizard: data, brand, workspace files, ready(), timeline().

Workspace files live in a content-addressed blob store; publishing and
every run snapshot the file list, so later edits never change a running
or shared result. The studio gets a Files tab and a widget inspector
with a live preview from sample data; agent steps can read the
workspace; MCP clients get list/read/write/delete_file and check_widget.

Generated HTML may run scripts, but only in an opaque origin with no
network: previews are sandboxed frames mounted once their HTML is
there, a CSP blocks every request, renders run in an offline browser
context, and the runtime re-fires resize for frames that get their
size late.

The architect is now a Mastra agent with tools: it edits the wizard
through the same ops as MCP, writes workspace files, downloads
reference data in one batch, reshapes it with run_script in an offline
browser, and checks the widget with a screenshot. The chat shows what
it is doing and says so when it runs out of steps.

Finished runs can be shared as /s/<token>: deliverables and downloads
only, never the answers, with a link to make your own. The share sheet
offers link, e-mail, X, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Facebook and the phone's
share menu; shared links get an Open Graph image. Runs of end users
without an account expire after RESULT_TTL_DAYS (7) and are purged
hourly.

commits.message:
feat: a database per tenant, model classes, sign-in at the Manage-App, phone inputs

Tenants: every tenant has its own libSQL database behind withTenant(); a control database
maps public links and run ids to their tenant and counts across tenants. tenant_id replaces
owner_id. Files live under the tenant's prefix, in the data folder or an S3 bucket.

Two ways to run: alone (one-time link, Host and Origin check, own keys, Ollama or a linked
account) and managed (MANAGE_URL: OIDC sign-in, tokens verified against the Manage-App's
JWKS, model calls through its gateway). Accounts, credits and Stripe left this repo.

Steps name a model class (classifier, standard, high, highest, image, video, audio) and an
effort hint. Cost per step is recorded; a run is estimated before it starts and its credits
are reserved.

Also: publish a local wizard to the cloud through the import API, studio chat on the Claude
subscription, sandbox engines behind one interface (Docker, agentOS), a cloud compose file
with a separate Chromium container, FSL-1.1-MIT.

Phones: camera with several shots and clips, code scan, location, voice notes, signature,
share sheet, wake lock, per-wizard home-screen entry, and the damage-report starter.

commits.message: installed AI clients as the model of a local runtime, first-start setup as a wizard
commits.body:
A runtime that runs alone can think through an AI client installed on the
machine, on the person's own subscription. Four clients are supported; each
runs headless as a model for the text classes, gets a step's tools over MCP
for the length of the call, and validates structured output itself where it
can.

- harness/: detection (version, sign-in), a per-client environment taken
  from the login shell with the subscription sign-in first, the headless
  calls, and the sign-in in a pseudo-terminal the studio shows inline
- mcp/bridge: a call's tools served over MCP; they run in the tenant
  context of the call that opened the bridge
- first start: the dev-login page is skipped where it is the only way in;
  the setup stays in front until a test call has worked on the chosen
  source. It opens with the choices alone, then shows what the choice needs
  (sign-in, keys, test) with colour-coded steps, a host per choice, a footer
  line and a layout for narrow screens
- language switch (EN/DE) in the setup and the user menu, applied in place
- settings: the source picker lists the installed clients; parts whose
  service is not there yet stay behind feature flags
- desktop bundle: the pty helper keeps its execute bit

commits.message: interactive widgets with a workspace per wizard, shareable results
commits.body:
Widgets are HTML apps written once into the wizard's workspace; a widget
step only binds each run's data into them — no model call, same look
every run. The result is one self-contained HTML file (scripts, styles,
images and reference data inlined) that previews, downloads and renders
to PNG, PDF and MP4 (the widget's timeline stepped frame by frame in
Chromium, encoded with ffmpeg). Widgets talk to the platform through
window.wizard: data, brand, workspace files, ready(), timeline().

Workspace files live in a content-addressed blob store; publishing and
every run snapshot the file list, so later edits never change a running
or shared result. The studio gets a Files tab and a widget inspector
with a live preview from sample data; agent steps can read the
workspace; MCP clients get list/read/write/delete_file and check_widget.

Generated HTML may run scripts, but only in an opaque origin with no
network: previews are sandboxed frames mounted once their HTML is
there, a CSP blocks every request, renders run in an offline browser
context, and the runtime re-fires resize for frames that get their
size late.

The architect is now a Mastra agent with tools: it edits the wizard
through the same ops as MCP, writes workspace files, downloads
reference data in one batch, reshapes it with run_script in an offline
browser, and checks the widget with a screenshot. The chat shows what
it is doing and says so when it runs out of steps.

Finished runs can be shared as /s/<token>: deliverables and downloads
only, never the answers, with a link to make your own. The share sheet
offers link, e-mail, X, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Facebook and the phone's
share menu; shared links get an Open Graph image. Runs of end users
without an account expire after RESULT_TTL_DAYS (7) and are purged
hourly.

commits.message: live studio — MCP and other edits show up without a reload
commits.body:
The editor subscribes to /api/studio/wizards/:id/stream. Every draft
write (studio, architect, MCP client) announces its revision and the
steps it touched; the editor fetches the new state, the changed steps
pulse in the diagram and the header names the client. Notes left by an
MCP client appear in the thread between turns.

Inspector edits still unsaved when another write lands are never lost:
their save meets the newer revision, the edits merge step by step onto
it (studio wins on the same step) and save again.

commits.message: OAuth sign-in for MCP clients, connected apps in settings
commits.body:
MCP clients connect without a key: they discover /api/mcp (RFC 9728),
register themselves (dynamic registration or a client metadata
document), the admin signs in and allows access on /consent, and the
client gets a token bound to /api/mcp. Tools follow the granted scopes.
Settings list connected apps; disconnecting removes the consent and the
tokens and cuts the app off at once. Personal API keys keep working.

Registrations with only loopback or custom-scheme redirects count as
native apps, so clients that leave application_type out still connect.

Includes migration 0002 of the workspace work, which 0003 builds on.

commits.message: MCP endpoint for authoring wizards with personal API keys
commits.body:
Admins build and change wizards from their own MCP clients. /api/mcp
(stateless Streamable HTTP, official SDK v2) offers 14 tools: authoring
guide, starters, projects, wizards, validate, create, edit ops, replace,
publish, sharing, test runs with answers, run reports with signed
download links. Personal API keys in Settings, rate-limited per key.

One service layer serves the studio routes and the MCP tools. Draft
writes carry a revision and refuse stale ones. MCP notes show up in the
studio thread. The architect and the MCP guide share one authoring text.
Architect turns that fail no longer leave their message behind; the
document preview frame renders again.
